text:
Rae K.: Proposal: tighten SIEM export access and introduce a formal unmask/unwrap protocol. Key points: short-lived export tokens (7d), JIT unwrap with ticket + approver (60m window), object-lock for audit logs, and an emergency soc-bypass that auto-revokes after 4h.

Sam - infra: +1. Implementation outline: export-proxy middleware validates token age/version, emits metrics `siem.export.token_age` and `siem.unwrap.events`. Dual-accept old tokens for 12d with warning header `X-Deprecated-Token: true`.

Priya (oncall): Rollout plan: staging -> internal consumers -> prod canary (10%) -> full. Need consumer healthcheck endpoint and migration notices to partners.

Anna - legal: Auditors require immutable approver + ticket id on every unwrap. Also require after-action report for any soc-bypass usage. Keep retention TTLs unchanged; this is access-only.

Rae K.: Example unwrap audit fields: timestamp, requester, role, key_id, ticket_id, approver, reason, duration_mins. Store to secure audit bucket (SSE-KMS) with object lock. Retention for audit entries = 7y.

Sam - infra: Alert rules: page if `unwrap_count(key) > 3 in 10m` or `unwrap_by_user > 5 in 1h`. Add Grafana panel. We'll add bucket-level write-once and restrict IAM to `audit-read` role only.

Priya (oncall): How do partners handle short-lived tokens? Many cache creds a week. Suggest 2-week dual-accept window and a migration email + SDK bump.

Rae K.: Action items: 1) Sam: PR for proxy middleware + alerts 2) Priya: test plan & canary run 3) Anna: draft compliance note for auditors 4) Rae: update RFC and runbook. I'll post the PR link when ready.

SOC Bot: Runbook published: https://runbooks.redwood.internal/siem/unmask-protocol — includes approver flow, soc-bypass conditions, and rollback steps.

Priya (oncall): I'll rehearse the flow in staging next shift and validate alert thresholds. :white_check_mark:
